SMTO-ART-0001 — SMTO couldn't get ready to save this step's files

GUID: df1f9152-ee74-4d0c-aa6e-68a65a7f4456
Slug: artifact-collection-unavailable
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • Before a step that can create files, SMTO gets ready to keep those files in the task's Artifacts. That preparation failed, so SMTO didn't run the step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check that the conversation is still in your conversation list and wasn't deleted, by you or by Auto-purge, while the task was running. SMTO can't keep files for a task whose conversation has been removed.
  2. Make sure the computer running SMTO has free disk space. Free space by removing unrelated files, not SMTO's own data folder. SMTO needs room in its data folder to record the files each step creates.
  3. Then select Continue task if the task shows it, or send your request again as a new message. This step never ran, so running it again won't do it twice.

What success looks like

  • The step runs, and any files it creates appear in the task's Artifacts.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete SMTO's data folder or old Artifacts to make room; they hold your conversations and saved files.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • ExecutionEngine could not initialize artifact collection (collector state lock, load or save, or the run's artifact workspace failed) before dispatching a file-producing capability, so it returned an undispatched artifact_collection_unavailable rejection.

What this means

  • ExecutionEngine cannot initialize artifact collection before capability dispatch and returns an explicitly undispatched rejection, preserving stronger proven Gateway admission errors separately. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • ExecutionEngine cannot initialize artifact collection before capability dispatch and returns an explicitly undispatched rejection, preserving stronger proven Gateway admission errors separately.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect collection initialization and the returned dispatched/executed facts before changing the target command.

How to fix it

  • Check the Server log for the exception raised by artifacts.collector.begin; typical causes are an unwritable or full Server state directory (AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR) or a retired or deleted artifact workspace for the run. Restore storage or start a new run; the rejected operation was not dispatched and can be retried once collection initializes.
  • Restore the owning workspace or Gateway and inspect storage availability before collecting again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported owning collection initializes and a new intended operation passes admission.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
